references.text: Pi-Hahiroth is mentioned again as the place where the Egyptians caught up with the Israelites, confirming the geographical location given in verse 2.
The Israelites' route through Pi-Hahiroth is repeated in the summary of the wilderness journey, confirming the campsite before Baal-Zephon.
Describes how God led the people toward the Sea of Reeds, providing context for why they were to camp by the sea.
Joshua reminds the people how their ancestors were brought out of Egypt and camped by the sea, where the Lord saved them from the Egyptians.
Describes the miraculous result of the Israelites camping by the sea—God parted the waters so they could walk through on dry ground.
This is the historical fulfillment of the command in Exodus 14:2; the same campsite pattern confirms God's guidance before the parting of the Red Sea.
